angle: Verify first, swap second: this issue's deck was rebuilt by its own fact-checkers — four combo claims ran the gauntlet before a single card moved, all four passed on the first attempt, and the seven surviving swaps turned a telegraphed vampire beatdown into the first deck in this series with a fully verified 2×2 matrix of table-kills, whose honest cost is that the whole pod can see it coming.

departments.headline: CAST EVERYTHING BUT HIM
departments.dek: What is the strongest card in a deck that begins every game with it face up and never pays a mana for it? Edgar Markov makes a Vampire for every Vampire you cast — from the command zone, from turn 1, for free — and version 2 changed what the banked bodies are for: the game that goes long is now, for the first time, your game.

callouts.title: BANK BODIES
callouts.text: Turns 1–3: deploy down the 8/18/18 curve of one-, two-, and three-drop Vampires. Every cast is two bodies — the creature and the eminence token — and the payoffs find themselves: a lord or Vampire payoff is drawn by turn 6 in 66.3% of simulated games. Do not cast Edgar. The engine costs nothing while he sits at home.

callouts.title: LAYER THE ENGINES
callouts.text: Turns 4–6: add what makes width lethal against three life totals — a drain engine (drawn by turn 6 in 62.7% of games), a token doubler (42.2%), and the new aristocrats layer: Viscera Seer, Cruel Celebrant, and Grave Pact turn every spare token into a scry, a table-wide drain, and an edict. Deploy under wrath-math — commit what wins, no further — knowing the sweep now costs the table almost as much as it costs you.

callouts.title: TAKE A WINDOW — YOU NOW HAVE TWO
callouts.text: Turn 6 and later, pick your kill. The attack turn: cast Edgar (median turn 6) into a protected seven-wide swing — 14 from every opponent at declare (stack 003), another 14 at your end step (stack 007, verified reach, not a kill), counters from Edgar's own trigger on top. Or the stack: tutor the missing half of the 2×2 loop matrix — and when the table holds open mana, fetch toward Sanguine Bond + Exquisite Blood, the pairing instant-speed creature removal cannot break.

captions.Edgar Markov: **THE ENGINE:** eminence makes a 1/1 Vampire per other Vampire spell you cast — while he is in the command zone. The deck's core engine is online before your first land drop and no removal spell in the format can touch it.
captions.Sanguine Bond: **THE NEW HALF:** Vito's trigger, word for word, on an enchantment — the swap that turned two verified loops into a 2×2 matrix of four. Verified before it was ever shuffled in.
captions.Viscera Seer: **THE OTHER NEW ENGINE:** one mana, instant-speed sacrifices, a scry per body — the card that makes every free eminence token worth something on its way out too.

pilot_tips.text: Never cast Edgar just because you hit six mana — cast him the turn you intend to swing wide with protection held, because his engine runs at full power from the zone and his body is the pivot, not the plan.

departments.pull_quote: The engine still costs zero. The long game now belongs to you too.

departments.headline: THE ZONE IS THE ENGINE
departments.dek: The command zone usually means guaranteed access to a card you still have to pay for. What is it worth when the ability works from the zone itself — and casting your commander is the optional part?
departments.body: Four teaching blocks and one coaching block. ONE — the guarantee, inverted (✓): eminence states its zones and functions from them (CR 113.6b), so this deck's engine is not merely guaranteed access — it is guaranteed operation. No mulligan finds it because no hand needs it; no removal answers it because no permanent carries it. TWO — the tax ladder (✓ CR 903.8): {3}{R}{W}{B} on the first cast, 8 on the second, 10 on the third — set beside the goldfish's mean available mana of 5.344 on turn 6 to show what each rung really costs this manabase. The wrinkle unique to this deck: recasting is genuinely optional, because a dead Edgar keeps making tokens from the zone — the tax buys back the alpha-strike trigger and the free-protection condition, nothing else. THREE — colour identity, with a scar to show (✓ CR 903.4): Mardu governs all 100 cards including lands' rules text, and this deck was caught by it at the border — the pilot's physical list arrived with Crosis's Catacombs, whose blue identity is illegal under Edgar; ingestion bounced it and Nomad Outpost took the slot at the pilot's direction (HISTORY.md). Print the catch proudly: the rule most players wave at is one this very issue enforced. FOUR — the clock (✓ CR 903.10a): 21 commander damage is a coincidence here, not a plan — the deck's real clocks are seven-wide drains, per-cast Purphoros burn, and four zero-mana loops. The coaching block (★) is protect-vs-race with the eminence twist: the free protection suite (Flawless Maneuver, Deflecting Swat at {0}) only switches on when Edgar resolves — so the insurance and the pivot arrive on the same turn, and before it, protection costs the exact mana the curve wants for Vampires. Budget accordingly.

captions.Edgar Markov: **THE COMMANDER FILE:** {3}{R}{W}{B}, Mardu identity, goldfish mean cast 6.628 (median 6, 51.2% by turn 6) — and an eminence ability that has been working since before turn 1.
captions.Flawless Maneuver: **PRICED IN EDGAR:** free only while you control a commander. The eminence plan keeps him zoned until turn 6, so this reads {2}{W} for the first five turns — the deck's central protection tension.
captions.Nomad Outpost: **THE LEGAL REPLACEMENT:** it holds the slot Crosis's Catacombs illegally occupied — a blue-identity land under a Mardu commander, caught at ingestion. Colour identity governs the 99, lands included.

pilot_tips.text: Count Deflecting Swat as part of Edgar's casting cost math — the turn he resolves, it flips from a three-mana trick to free interaction, which is a real argument for an earlier Edgar against a known combo seat.

departments.pull_quote: Removal cannot touch the command zone. The table's only answer to eminence is to end the game.

departments.headline: THE BODY COUNT
departments.dek: Ten thousand seeded runs, no opponents, no mercy: what does a zero-mana engine actually produce, how often does the loop matrix assemble itself, and why does a six-drop commander still have a median cast of turn 6? The chart answers all three — and names the tempo tax the manabase pays.

callouts.title: BODIES WITHOUT A COMMANDER
callouts.text: Mean bodies: 1.766 by turn 3, 4.111 by turn 6, 6.354 by turn 10 — with zero mana ever spent on Edgar. That is the eminence dividend, and the model doesn't even count doubler multiplication beyond parsed token text.

callouts.title: MEDIAN CAST: TURN 6
callouts.text: Edgar lands by turn 6 in 51.2% of games (mean 6.628); the histogram's spike is turn 6 at 3,764 of 10,000 runs, and 1,656 runs never cast him by turn 10 — losing nothing but the alpha strike for it.

callouts.title: THE 5.4% MATRIX
callouts.text: A loop pair — any lose-half plus any gain-half — assembles naturally in 5.4% of games by turn 6 and 9.4% by turn 10. Four halves make every draw step live, but read the number honestly: the matrix is tutored into existence far more often than it is drawn, and the three tutors are not modeled here at all.

callouts.title: THE TAPPED-LAND TAX
callouts.text: 16 of 34 lands can enter tapped; land drops fall to 58.2% by turn 6 and mean available mana is 5.344 — which is the whole story of why a six-mana commander waits. The curve lives at one, two, and three on purpose, and Herald's Horn's rebate (ramp-or-fixing drawn: 50.2% by turn 6) is the swap that eases it.

captions.Herald's Horn: **LAB NOTE:** cost reducers, rituals, and tutors are not modeled — every figure on this page is the floor. The real deck casts more, drains more, and completes the matrix more often than the chart admits.

pilot_tips.text: Lead Ancient Tomb into a two-drop Vampire whenever the opener offers it — two colourless on turn 1 is a body plus a banked eminence token before anyone else has moved.

departments.pull_quote: Half the games cast Edgar by turn 6. Every game runs his engine from turn 1.
departments.note: The stated-assumptions box is non-negotiable and earns its keep twice here: the model simulates resource development, not games (no interaction, no removal), and it does not model the tutor suite — so 5.4%/9.4% is natural assembly only, exactly as the strategic frame frames it. Cite every number exactly as goldfish_metrics.json v2 reports: 0.512, 6.628, median 6, 1.766, 4.111, 6.354, 0.582, 5.344, 0.054, 0.094, 0.663, 0.627, 0.575, 0.506, 0.502, 0.422, 0.817, 0.219, histogram 3764, not_by_max_turn 1656. Seed 42, 10,000 iterations. Do NOT print v1 deltas as data (the v1 goldfish no longer exists as an artifact); if the velocity-for-kill-web trade is mentioned, attribute it to the strategic frame in coaching voice.

departments.headline: EIGHT FILES, THREE MOVEMENTS
departments.dek: An overture, a matrix, and an attack turn scored twice. Eight case files, every one checker-passed against the June 19, 2026 rules — including the four that ran BEFORE their cards were shuffled in, and the one that came back stamped 'not a table-kill.' We print that one just as large.

callouts.title: OVERTURE: FIVE BODIES, TWO MANA
callouts.text: Stack 002, the everyday engine: a two-mana Vampire cast with Edgar zoned and both doublers out. Eminence triggers once, Anointed Procession and Mondrak double it in either order — 1 becomes 2 becomes 4, the checker confirmed order doesn't matter — and all four tokens enter with Socialite counters. Five new bodies, one cast, and tokens are created, not cast, so eminence never re-triggers on them. Every other file on these pages runs on this arithmetic. FULL DOSSIER: JUDGE'S DESK A-002 →

callouts.title: THE MATRIX: 38 TRIGGERS
callouts.text: Stack 001, the marquee corner: Exquisite Blood plus Vito, seeded by an ordinary 2-point lifelink hit. Each Vito trigger is a new object targeted fresh, so you walk the drain across the table — 6, 13, and 19 resolutions clear opponents at 12, 25, and 38 life, 38 iterations total, and a mid-loop death never breaks the chain because the killing loss still triggers your enchantment. You end at 105 life having spent nothing. FULL DOSSIER: JUDGE'S DESK A-001 →

callouts.title: THE MATRIX: THE UNTOUCHABLE CORNER
callouts.text: Stack 005, verified before its card was swapped in: Sanguine Bond plus Exquisite Blood — both enchantments. From a 2-life seed, 26 Bond resolutions clear the table (9, then 17), the chain crosses the first opponent's death, and you win by rule 104.2a at 79 life. The reason this is the corner to tutor toward when the table holds open mana: there is no creature in the loop, so the per-iteration removal window the other corners must confess to simply does not exist. FULL DOSSIER: JUDGE'S DESK A-005 →

callouts.title: THE MATRIX: THE FRAGILE TWIN
callouts.text: Stack 004: Bloodthirsty Conqueror's trigger matches Exquisite Blood's word for word — the checker confirmed '(Damage causes loss of life.)' is reminder text, not a requirement — and 13 iterations from a 3-life seed killed a 9- and a 30-life opponent with zero overkill. The honest cost at full size: the gain half is a 5/5 creature, so every iteration's priority window admits instant-speed removal. FULL DOSSIER: JUDGE'S DESK A-004 →

callouts.title: THE MATRIX: CLOSING THE SQUARE
callouts.text: Stack 006: Sanguine Bond plus Bloodthirsty Conqueror, 13 Bond resolutions from a 3-life seed (4, then 9, each overkilling by exactly 1 because 3 divides neither total). One creature half means one removal target per iteration — fewer than 004's pairing, more than 005's zero. Four corners, four stamps: whichever half the tutor finds first, you already know what completes it. FULL DOSSIER: JUDGE'S DESK A-006 →

callouts.title: ATTACK TURN, PART ONE: FOURTEEN AT DECLARE
callouts.text: Stack 003, the fair kill: seven Vampires attack with Sanctum Seeker and Bloodletter of Aclazotz among them. Seven Seeker triggers, each opponent's loss doubled on your turn: 14 from every opponent at declare attackers, before a single blocker is named — and the checker confirmed the opponent at 14 hits exactly 0 and is gone by state-based actions mid-combat. Your gain is 7, never doubled: Bloodletter reads opponents only. FULL DOSSIER: JUDGE'S DESK A-003 →

callouts.title: ATTACK TURN, PART TWO: THE ECHO THAT ISN'T A KILL
callouts.text: Stack 007, the honest file: the same seven attackers, now tapped, plus Throne of the God-Pharaoh. At your end step each opponent loses 7 — doubled by Bloodletter to 14, who stayed home untapped and so does not count itself. Verified — and PARTIALLY REFUTED as a table-kill, in the artifact's own words: a 15-life opponent survives at exactly 1. The 28-per-opponent full-turn figure is arithmetic composed from two separately verified files, not one checker-passed line. Present it as reach, never as lethal-by-default. FULL DOSSIER: JUDGE'S DESK A-007 →

callouts.title: ATTACK TURN, PART THREE: TEN PER HEAD, PER CAST
callouts.text: Stack 008: with Purphoros and both doublers out, one two-mana Vampire cast is four simultaneous token entries — four separate Purphoros triggers, the checker confirmed — plus a fifth when the spell's own body arrives. Five triggers, 2 damage each, to every opponent: 10 per head per cast, no combat required, and the verified line's opponent at 10 hit exactly 0 on the fifth resolution. FULL DOSSIER: JUDGE'S DESK A-008 →

captions.Vito, Thorn of the Dusk Rose: **LOSE-HALF ONE:** every life gain becomes targeted loss — the hinge of matrix corners 001 and 004, and the deck's most removal-magnetic card. Sanguine Bond exists because he dies on sight.
captions.Sanguine Bond: **LOSE-HALF TWO:** the same trigger on an enchantment Swords can't reach — verified with both gain-halves (stacks 005 and 006) before the swap that shuffled it in was ever applied.
captions.Exquisite Blood: **GAIN-HALF ONE:** the resilient enchantment half; with Sanguine Bond it forms the matrix's only corner with no creature in the loop at all.
captions.Bloodthirsty Conqueror: **GAIN-HALF TWO:** the same words on a 5/5 flying deathtouch body — a removal window every iteration, and a fair-game monster the loop never needs.
captions.Purphoros, God of the Forge: **THE CAST TAX:** 10 to every opponent per two-mana Vampire through both doublers — indestructible, and usually not a creature, so the wrath your tokens invite doesn't touch him.

pilot_tips.text: Never wait for a big lifegain event to start a loop — stacks 001 and 005 were both seeded by an ordinary 2-point lifelink connect, and any lifelink body in the 99 can supply it.

departments.pull_quote: Four loops, one table — and the resilient corner never puts a creature on the stack.
departments.note: The issue's peak and the heaviest Kill this series has run: stage it as three movements, not eight equal spreads. Movement one (A-002) is the overture at feature scale. Movement two is the centerpiece: a literal 2×2 grid spread — rows are lose-halves (Vito, Sanguine Bond), columns are gain-halves (Exquisite Blood, Bloodthirsty Conqueror) — with kill counts 38/13/26/13 printed in each cell and the four callouts (n2–n5) anchoring the corners; per-corner removal-window glyphs teach the sequencing skill. Movement three (A-003 → A-007 → A-008) walks one attack turn chronologically: declare, end step, and the cast that preceded it all. The pull quote runs full-width between movements two and three as the lung. Map-key carries ♥ life and a token glyph. 007's refutation panel is the honesty beat — same size as the wins. Copy discipline: stacks 001/005 were seeded by 'Vampire Nighthawk's lifelink' and 002/008 cast 'Gifted Aetherborn' — both cards are now on the bench, so the department's own copy says 'a 2-point lifelink hit' and 'a two-mana Vampire' (the math is card-agnostic and the artifacts remain valid rules records); Judge's Desk prints the artifacts verbatim, props and all, and a one-line note there explains the prop moved to the bench after verification.

departments.headline: ARCHENEMY, IN WRITING
departments.dek: Eminence banks a visible body from turn 1, and your deck now contains the four most famous drain pairings in the format. When your threat level is structural and everybody has read the same combo database, what does table-talk even buy — and which window do you actually protect?

callouts.title: THREAT WINDOW
callouts.text: The board state that flips you to archenemy: any visible loop half next to open black mana — and the strategic frame is blunt that with roughly 355,000 combined database entries across your four pairings, the deflection budget is largely pre-spent by seat assignment. Deflection buys single turns now, not phases. Spend those turns on purpose.

callouts.title: THE OPEN SECRET
callouts.text: At a bracket-4 floor, sandbagging four famous combos reads as bad faith, not cleverness — the frame says play the kill-web honestly as a co-equal plan. Honesty is not surrender: declare the deck, then make the table solve the sequencing. A lone Exquisite Blood or Conqueror still reads as value and passively feeds on all table damage; the moment a second complementary half is visible, you are the archenemy on the clock.

callouts.title: SEQUENCE BY REMOVAL WINDOW
callouts.text: The real concealment is which corner you present. Your tutors put the missing half where no removal reaches — hand and library — so fetch toward the pairing the table's open mana cannot answer: against held creature removal, Sanguine Bond + Exquisite Blood (stack 005, no creature in the loop); the creature corners only when the answer-holders are tapped out. Complete the pair in the dead window, never into it.

captions.Demonic Tutor: **THE ARMOR:** the table knows what a tutor with a loop half on board means — but an assumption is not a target, and a card in hand cannot be Dispatched.
captions.Grave Pact: **THE RESENTMENT ENGINE:** every token death forces each opponent to sacrifice — and Viscera Seer now supplies those deaths on demand. Value that makes enemies; fire it while your deflection budget still has a balance.
captions.Kalitas, Traitor of Ghet: **THE QUIET GRUDGE:** exiling everything the table's creatures do when they die — and minting you Zombies for it — is the kind of card opponents remember. He anchors your defense; expect him to draw the removal your loop halves didn't.

pilot_tips.text: Cast Exquisite Blood while it still reads as a lifegain trinket — alone it draws no removal, it feeds on every point of damage anywhere at the table, and once it's down only the cheap half of two different loops is ever exposed again.

departments.pull_quote: You cannot sandbag four famous combos. Wear the label — and make the table answer the right corner.

departments.headline: PIVOT OR PATIENCE
departments.dek: One turn asks whether six mana is Edgar or two more Vampires; the other asks what a tutor is really for when everyone at the table knows what you'd fetch. Read each board, commit out loud, and only then read the bench's ruling.

callouts.title: HOW TO PLAY ALONG
callouts.text: Cover the recommendation box. Read the board, pick a branch, say it out loud — the signals and coalition risks are printed with each branch so you can argue with them. Being wrong on this page is free; being wrong at the table costs a game.

callouts.title: TURN 6: THE ALPHA WINDOW
callouts.text: Decision 001. Six mana after the Knight resolves, four banked tokens, a draw-go player with four untapped lands, an aggro seat at 12 and tapped out. Edgar now, a bigger board, or a smaller board with protection held? Every branch is defensible. One is right.

callouts.title: TURN 8: THE HIDDEN HALF
callouts.text: Decision 002. Vito survived a full rotation, Demonic Tutor in hand, eight lands untapped — and the control seat has held five mana all game. Fetch and present, fetch and hide, or hold the tutor as an answer? Four verified corners say the kill is real; the question is whether this is its window.

captions.Swiftfoot Boots: **THE QUIET ENABLER:** hexproof plus haste for one to equip is the difference between an Edgar who pivots the game and an Edgar who eats the removal the table saved six turns for.

pilot_tips.text: Ask which wrath you actually fear before leaning on Flawless Maneuver — indestructible beats destroy effects, and does nothing against Toxic Deluge's -X/-X or an exile sweeper.

departments.pull_quote: An assumption is not a target.
departments.note: Render both decision artifacts in full — board, question, all branches with signals and coalition risk, recommendation revealed only after the branches, per the artifact contract. Both were re-derived against the v2 list and figures (002 cites the 9.4%-by-turn-10 assembly). Neither headline nor callout may telegraph a recommendation; 'PIVOT OR PATIENCE' names the tension, not the answer. Decision 002 is the sequencing doctrine's teaching home — the politics spread points here.

departments.headline: WHO DRAINS THE DRAINER
departments.dek: The sweeper is near-certain over four players, the taxes halve your two-spell turns, and a single 'players can't gain life' effect now switches off all FOUR loops at once. But which layer of your deck survives each of these — and can you name your outs before you sit down?

threats.read: The wrath now costs them more than it costs you. Grave Pact and Cruel Celebrant convert the board they sweep into edicts and each-opponent drains, Viscera Seer cashes tokens at instant speed in response, the two enchantment halves and an indestructible (and usually noncreature) Purphoros survive outright, and eminence rebuilds at one token per cast with no recast tax — Bloodghast for free on a land drop. Commit only what wins before the sweep; the v1 advice to fear the long game is repealed, because four verified corners are inevitability. The unrebuildable loss is Edgar himself: the next cast is 8.

Know exactly which layer dies: 'players can't gain life' turns off the ENTIRE 2×2 matrix — every corner needs a gain-half to fire — and blanks the lifelink bodies. But your hate-proof plan is verified three ways: Sanctum Seeker's each-opponent trigger doubled by Bloodletter is life LOSS (stack 003's 14 at declare), Throne's end-step echo is life loss (stack 007's 14, reach not kill), and Purphoros deals damage with no lifegain anywhere in sight (stack 008's 10 per cast). Stop tutoring for gain-halves; start tutoring for the hate's answer — or for Purphoros, who never noticed the hate was there.

You are the forced beatdown: the 18-and-18 two/three-drop core is exactly the many-cheap-spells profile that Sphere effects halve, and your mana is already taxed — 16 of 34 lands enter tapped and mean available mana is 5.344 on turn 6. Race the lock's assembly and aim removal at the one piece that beats YOU (usually the per-cast tax, since eminence pays per cast). Two hedges the swaps bought: Herald's Horn rebates one generic mana on nearly every spell you cast, and the loops are notably tax-resistant once assembled — every corner needs zero mana to iterate. Edgar stays zoned longest here.

Answer economy inverts: the last profitable moment for held interaction is now. But your counter-clock is materially faster than it was — four corners, three tutors, and 5.4%-by-turn-6 natural assembly mean the tutored kill is usually one turn away once either half sticks. The white removal and Deflecting Swat protect that turn, with the standing tension that Swat is free only once Edgar resolves — a real argument for an earlier, unprotected Edgar against a known combo seat. Present the kill first, and prefer presenting the all-enchantment corner.

pilot_tips.text: Feed Bloodghast to Viscera Seer, Diabolic Intent, and Grave Pact without hesitation — it can't block anyway, and it returns on any land drop, fetch cracks included.
Cast Olivia's Wrath as an attack, not a rescue — with a wide Vampire board its -X/-X clears every blocker and misses your entire army.

departments.pull_quote: The hate card turns off all four loops at once — and leaves the declare-step drain, the end-step echo, and the god untouched. Life loss isn't lifegain.
departments.note: The aggro archetype from the frame folds into the coaching around the boxes if space demands, but prefer keeping four boxes as listed — the lifegain-hate box is the department's teaching peak because the matrix made the hate card table-correct. Honest v2 cost, printed: the swaps benched two deathtouch walls, so against creature aggro your control seat is held with drains, edicts, and Kalitas rather than blockers — Vampire of the Dire Moon is the last one-drop deathtouch defender.

departments.headline: EVERY CAST COUNTS TWICE
departments.dek: Sixty-three spells whose common cost is hidden: each Vampire cast also prints a body from the command zone. The four-corner kill matrix and its three couriers lead, the new aristocrats layer converts the tokens, and a manabase hauling 50 black pips closes — with the twelve slots the role taxonomy famously cannot see, named in print.

captions.Viscera Seer: **THE CONVERTER:** the deck's one true sac outlet — each free token becomes a Grave Pact edict, a Cruel Celebrant drain, and a scry, at instant speed, on demand.

departments.pull_quote: Twenty-nine threats, one sweeper of your own, and an engine no wrath can reach.
departments.note: Rank matters: the matrix leads because it is why the bracket floor reads 4; mana closes. Full card blurbs render from manual_prose.card_roles (v2-synced) — the remaining 25 lands beyond the marked-cards group render there. The 34-card physical sideboard renders as its own labeled strip (this deck's accessories are a bench, not tokens), pointing to Upgrade Watch for the rulings. No synergy-graph claim appears anywhere (1 intra-deck edge; it is a global shortlist, not a fit score).

departments.headline: NINETY-THREE HANDS
departments.dek: Who gets the credit page when ninety-three artists split 131 cards and the leaders hold four apiece? Nobody — and that's the story. This collection was assembled card by card across a decade of printings, so the feature follows the deck's own plot: the hand that painted the attack turn.

featured.note: Two entries, two copies, no inflation — and they happen to be both halves of this deck's signature turn: Bloodletter of Aclazotz, the doubler that now anchors TWO verified case files (stack 003's 14 at declare, stack 007's 14 at the end step), and Akroma's Will, the spell that makes the same alpha strike unanswerable. One artist, by pure collection accident, painted the attack turn and its protection — and the seven swaps only deepened the coincidence, promoting Throne of the God-Pharaoh to stand exactly where his bat god's doubling matters twice a turn. In a 93-artist book, that is the closest thing to a byline the swing turn will ever get.

also_worth_noting.note: Co-leader at four entries — and after the swaps, all four are in the 99: Castle Locthwain, Luxury Suite, Savai Triome, and the newly promoted Throne of the God-Pharaoh. The manabase's house painter now also painted the issue's freshly verified end-step echo.

The other co-leader at four entries, and the swaps' quiet counterweight: Arcane Signet and Diabolic Intent hold maindeck slots while Akroma's Memorial and Leering Onlooker sit on the bench. Two shelves, one hand.
Three entries, all maindeck, all nocturnes — Blood Crypt, Silent Clearing, Twilight Prophet. The deck's mood board in three frames.

Two entries — both of them Vito, Thorn of the Dusk Rose, in different printings: the maindeck hinge of two verified loops, and its spare in the box. Painting the deck's most removal-magnetic card twice is its own kind of credit.

captions.Bloodletter of Aclazotz: **THE DOUBLER, SIGNED:** Manzanedo's bat god presides over two case files — 7 becomes 14 at declare attackers (stack 003), and 7 becomes 14 again at your end step (stack 007).
captions.Akroma's Will: **THE SHIELD, SAME HAND:** Manzanedo also painted the swing turn's protection — with Edgar on the battlefield you take both modes, and every lifelink point it grants is a lose-half trigger.

departments.note: The analysis reports no standout (lead artists hold 4 entries; its own note says tell a breadth story) and an empty drop-run list, so no bought-whole caveat applies: this concentration pattern is honest breadth, not structure. Scope note for the Art File box, printed: the census covers the pilot's full collection — the 99 plus the 34-card bench, 131 entries and 136 copies across 93 artists. Respect the per-entry notes verbatim: Swamp is 1 entry/4 copies (per-copy would inflate Dimitar Marinski), Unholy Officiant and Vampire Nocturnus are 1 entry/2 copies each. Remaining Art File facts: 1 borderless, 0 foils, 20 legendary frames, 9 showcases. The featured pick is editorial — chosen for the story, counts recomputed by the renderer.

departments.headline: NEVER KEEP FOR EDGAR
departments.dek: 81.7% of first sevens are keeps at 0.219 mulligans per game — and your commander is none of the reason. He's face up in the zone before your first decision, so the drill is pure engine-hand arithmetic: enablers over payoffs, untapped over tapped, and the seductive new trap — a fistful of loop halves — shipped without mercy.

hands.why: Three lands that can all enter untapped, two one-mana Vampires (each worth two bodies), a lord, and a refill. This is the enabler-heavy shape that wins the engine-hand test — the payoffs find themselves: a lord or payoff is drawn by turn 6 in 66.3% of games.

Two lands reads risky until you price the mana: Tomb into Ring is four mana of ramp on turn 1, and Herald's Horn discounts every body behind it while digging at each upkeep. The deck-facts nuance that saves this keep — 16 of 34 lands can enter tapped, so a two-land hand needs its lands untapped. These are.

cards: Vito, Thorn of the Dusk Rose
hands.why: Three loop halves in one opener feels like destiny — and it is the classic all-payoff mulligan the frame warns about: no play before turn 3, the entire eminence dividend skipped, and your kill telegraphed from the first discard. Natural assembly runs 5.4% by turn 6 without any help, and the tutors are the real copies. Enablers are the thing an opener must actually hold.

hands.verdict: SHIP — the flood the sim would keep
hands.why: The goldfish's mechanical rule keeps 2–5 lands, so this five-lander passes the machine — and the coach overrules it. One spell to cast before turn 4, and protection plus a tutor are luxuries in an opener, not a plan. The badge difference printed honestly: ◆ says keepable, ★ says ship.

captions.Concealed Courtyard: **THE FIRST-THREE-TURNS LAND:** untapped exactly through the land drops when an 8-one-drop, 18-two-drop curve needs it most.

pilot_tips.text: Grade one-drops on casts, not stats — Viscera Seer on turn 1 is a body, a banked eminence token, and a machine that will out-value most rares in this deck by turn 8.

departments.pull_quote: He lives in the command zone. Mulligan like he doesn't exist.

departments.headline: THE BENCH, AFTER THE RAID
departments.dek: Last issue's bench analysis didn't stay analysis: four case files ran, four passed, and seven cards walked into the 99 with verification stamps in hand. What's left is a true sideboard — two conditionals with named triggers, a recall shelf the swaps knowingly created, and one card that can never legally play.

callouts.title: THE RAID, ON THE RECORD
callouts.text: The order is the story: the old analysis claimed four unverified interactions — the two Sanguine Bond loops, Throne under Bloodletter, and Purphoros's per-entry count — so the verifications ran FIRST. All four passed the checker at iteration 1 (stacks 005–008, with 007's honest not-a-table-kill bound), and only then did the seven swaps land: Viscera Seer, Sanguine Bond, Cruel Celebrant, Purphoros, Kalitas, Herald's Horn, and Throne in; Interloper, Stensia Masquerade, Gifted Aetherborn, Akroma's Memorial, Vampire Nighthawk, Ivora, and Blade of the Bloodchief to the bench. Every delta computed 4-to-4: the floor never moved, because the purchase was redundancy on the kill and velocity to reach it.

callouts.title: CONDITIONAL: ELENDA
callouts.text: Elenda, the Dusk Rose in for Mavren Fein, Dusk Apostle — once real games show the Seer/Celebrant/Grave Pact web generating multiple deaths per turn cycle. She collects a counter from every death anywhere and dies into a doubled army of lifelink tokens, each entry a verified 2-damage Purphoros trigger (stack 008). A payoff without its engine is a 4-mana 1/1; let the engine prove its tempo first.

callouts.title: CONDITIONAL: THE NINTH SWAP
callouts.text: Indulgent Aristocrat in for Vampire of the Dire Moon — outlet redundancy, adopted only if Viscera Seer keeps dying before the web fires AND your pods aren't punishing the loss of the last one-mana deathtouch blocker. This is the swap most likely to be reversed by the aggro matchup, and the analysis says so in exactly those words. Nearby on the recall shelf: Gifted Aetherborn and Vampire Nighthawk, benched deathtouch walls whose return case is written for the day fair combat starts connecting.

callouts.title: NEVER: RUNO STROMKIRK
callouts.text: The bench's one unplayable card: {1}{U}{B} — blue identity, illegal under a Mardu commander, the same rule that bounced Crosis's Catacombs at ingestion. It lives in the box as a collection card, and printing that plainly is the point. Also not options: the spare Vito, Strefan, Nocturnus, and Officiant copies — backups, not upgrades.

captions.Elenda, the Dusk Rose: **THE HELD PAYOFF:** a counter from every death anywhere, then a doubled army of lifelink tokens on her way out — benched until the maindeck death engine proves it feeds her.
captions.Indulgent Aristocrat: **THE NINTH SWAP:** a second one-mana outlet whose activations pump the tribe — waiting on evidence that one outlet isn't enough, and priced in the deck's last cheap deathtouch body.

pilot_tips.text: When you weigh future sac-outlet swaps, remember Kalitas is already your second outlet — the role taxonomy doesn't count his ability, but your spare tokens and his +1/+1 counters do.

departments.pull_quote: Verify first, apply the survivors — the floor never moved, and that was never the point.
departments.note: Source is sideboard_analysis.json (post-swap bookkeeping pass) plus HISTORY.md line 3 — this issue's Upgrade Watch reads the pilot's own bench rather than the obsolescence index, and says so. The pilot's recorded mandate (pilot_feedback.md) colours the voice: always slightly more aggressive, engine-extenders over sidegrades — so the two candidate stack scenarios still open (Grave Pact × Kalitas replacement interaction; Cruel Celebrant loop-ignition ordering) are teased here as 'the next two files worth commissioning,' flagged plainly as needs-a-stack-scenario, never asserted. Also name the depth shelf honestly in one paragraph: Master of Dark Rites is first in when a slot opens, Markov Purifier first if the pilot reports running out of gas — verdicts from the analysis, not new judgment.

departments.headline: EIGHT FILES, EIGHT STAMPS
departments.dek: The 2×2 matrix in four files, the token math, the attack turn at both ends, and the burn count — every citation verbatim against the June 19, 2026 comprehensive rules. One file needed a second attempt, and one came back stamped 'not a table-kill.' We tell you which, because that's the whole point of this desk.
departments.note: Renderer-generated from the eight checker-passed artifacts; nothing summarized, truncated, or paraphrased. Case order A-001 through A-008 with verdict and iteration count as case status — A-003 passed on iteration 2 (the near-miss is credibility, not embarrassment); all others passed on iteration 1, including the four commissioned BEFORE their cards were swapped in (A-005 through A-008 — the file tabs carry a small 'VERIFIED PRE-SWAP' annotation, which is this issue's proudest piece of paperwork). A-007's status line must carry its own artifact's language: verified as a 14-per-opponent end-step drain, PARTIALLY REFUTED as a table-kill. One-line prop note on A-001/A-002/A-005/A-008: the scenario's seed and cast cards (Vampire Nighthawk, Gifted Aetherborn) moved to the bench after verification — the rules findings are card-agnostic and stand as written. Manila, stamps, typewriter face throughout.

Next issue is TO BE ANNOUNCED per issue.json — run the teaser as authored, do not invent a deck. Colophon: rules version June 19, 2026; decklist sha256 6047837e800e…; goldfish seed 42, 10,000 iterations. Fan Content Policy line. Provenance paragraph closes the loop with the issue's honest origin story, now in two acts: ingestion caught Crosis's Catacombs — a blue-identity land illegal under Edgar, replaced by Nomad Outpost at the pilot's direction — and the version-2 revision inverted the usual order of operations: four stack scenarios were commissioned against bench cards, all four passed, and only then were the seven swaps applied (HISTORY.md, 2026-07-28). The border control worked, the fact-checkers picked the cards, and printing both is the same house style that prints refutations: our credibility is the checker.

rhythm_notes: The canonical order still alternates cleanly, but The Kill at eight files is the heaviest this series has run, so its internal structure IS the rhythm: three movements (overture → matrix → attack turn) rather than eight equal spreads, with the full-width pull quote as a lung between the matrix grid and the attack-turn chronology, and 007's refutation panel as a tonal beat that resets attention before 008 closes the movement. By the Numbers (dense analysis) hands off to The Kill's narrative opening, not its grid. Politics (reflection) decompresses into the participatory decision spreads; Know Your Enemy (reference) is followed by two low-intensity browse departments — The 99 and Featured Artist — before Keep or Ship brings the reader back to practice; Upgrade Watch and Judge's Desk taper to the opt-in deep end (the Desk is long at eight cases, but it is reference by design and opt-in by placement), and the back page closes on provenance rather than running out of artifacts. Pun budget spent, all in furniture: 'the drill, with teeth' (contents blurb), 'THE BODY COUNT' (data headline, literal enough to earn its keep), 'bad blood, good paperwork' (contents blurb for the Desk), and 'THE BENCH, AFTER THE RAID' (department headline). Four, and stopping.
gaps: Two candidate lines remain unverified and are flagged, never asserted: the Grave Pact edict into Kalitas's exile-replacement interaction, and the Cruel Celebrant loop-ignition ordering (a death seeding an assembled pair) — one resolve-stack run each settles them, and both are named as 'the next two files' in Upgrade Watch.

Stacks 001 and 005 seed their loops with Vampire Nighthawk and stacks 002 and 008 cast Gifted Aetherborn — both cards moved to the bench AFTER verification. The artifacts remain valid rules records and Judge's Desk prints them verbatim with a one-line prop note; department copy uses card-agnostic phrasing ('a 2-point lifelink hit', 'a two-mana Vampire'). Re-staging with maindeck props would be cosmetic but would remove the caveat.

The goldfish does not model the tutor suite, so 5.4%/9.4% pair assembly is natural draw only and understates practical assembly everywhere it appears; a tutor-aware target would ground the 'co-equal plan' framing numerically.
